statedReasoning: Per the fully-fetched bill text and důvodová zpráva (submitted 16 Jan 2026 by the same seven-MP group as tisk 71 — Richterová, Bartoš, Ančincová, Pipášová, Martínková Španihelová, Šmída, Volpe), this bill amends zákon č. 427/2011 Sb. with a DIFFERENT, disjoint set of provisions from tisk 71: it inserts new definitions of 'fond soukromého kapitálu' (private-equity fund) and 'fond rizikového kapitálu' (venture-capital fund) into §3 (new písm. w) and x)); adds a new §98 odst. 1 písm. g) allowing the mandatory conservative fund (povinný konzervativní fond) to hold equities/comparable securities traded on an EU-regulated or OECD-member-state-regulated market (previously excluded — the conservative fund's investment universe was almost entirely fixed-income); makes the conforming change in §98 odst. 3; and adds a new §100 odst. 2 písm. k) plus a new §100 odst. 8, allowing ordinary účastnické fondy (participant funds) to invest in securities issued by PE/VC funds up to a hard cap of 10% of fund assets. Stated rationale: Czech third-pillar pension assets (658.8 bn Kč per ČNB, Q3 2025) are invested unusually conservatively versus OECD peers; the reform aims to improve long-term risk-adjusted returns given demographic pressure (rising pensioner ratio, cited to ČSÚ population projections and the EU's 2024 Ageing Report), while keeping prudential guardrails (regulated-market listing requirement for equities in the conservative fund; a hard 10% PE/VC ceiling for participant funds; CNB supervision unchanged). Stated fiscal impact: NONE on the state budget — the DZ frames this as a private-market prudential-investment-limit change with only indirect, unquantified long-term effects on saver returns and potentially the Czech capital market (citing Invest Europe data that pension funds supply ~19% of European PE fundraising). Effective date proposed: 1 January 2027.
researchedContext: Legislative history confirms the bill was distributed as print 86/0 on 22 Jan 2026, and — unlike sibling tisk 71's NEUTRAL government position — received a government 'nesouhlas' (disapproval), distributed as print 86/1 on 25 Feb 2026, a distinction plausibly linked to this bill's more consequential prudential change (opening the mandatory conservative fund — the default, most risk-averse product in the system — to equity and PE/VC-adjacent exposure) versus tisk 71's pure fee-ceiling cut. The Organizational Committee recommended proceeding 4 Mar 2026 (rapporteur Ing. Benjamin Činčila, Budget Committee as guarantor); as of 24 July 2026 the bill remains at this pre-first-reading stage with one amendment pending. SIBLING-COLLISION CHECK (tisk 71 ↔ tisk 86, both amending 427/2011, per this batch's brief): having read both bill texts in full, there is NO textual or provision-level overlap. Tisk 71 touches §60 odst. 3, §60 odst. 4, and §192 odst. 3 písm. a) (fee ceilings). Tisk 86 touches §3 (new definitions), §98 odst. 1 and 3 (conservative-fund investment universe), and §100 odst. 2 and a new odst. 8 (participant-fund PE/VC allowance). Zero shared paragraphs, zero renumbering conflicts, zero contradictory instructions — unlike batch-001's genuine tisk 120/244 §35ba collision, this is a clean case of the same sponsor group splitting one broader third-pillar reform agenda into two independently-progressing, non-colliding bills (fee reform vs. investment-liberalization reform) rather than an uncoordinated duplication or drafting error.

unstatedEffects.effect: Allowing participant funds to hold up to 10% of assets in PE/VC fund securities, and the mandatory conservative fund to hold listed equities for the first time, creates a new institutional distribution channel into third-pillar retirement savings for private-equity and venture-capital fund managers generally — a class of financial intermediary that did not previously have statutory access to this pool of state-subsidized savings. The DZ presents this as a saver-return benefit but does not name or quantify which PE/VC managers might benefit, nor does it address the added illiquidity, valuation-lag, and fee-layering risk (J-curve effect) it itself acknowledges for savers defaulted into the 'conservative' fund who did not choose equity exposure.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: PE/VC fund managers gain a new institutional-capital access channel; savers (including risk-averse savers automatically enrolled in the mandatory conservative fund) bear new equity/illiquidity risk exposure they may not have selected.

conflictAssessment: No plausible self-dealing channel. As with sibling tisk 71, none of the seven sponsors holds a recorded money tie to a pension company, asset manager, or PE/VC fund manager. Lenka Martínková Španihelová's MATURUS, o.p.s. tie is a disability-employment nonprofit (o.p.s. legal form, structurally incapable of being a 'penzijní společnost, a.s.' or an investment fund under Czech law), unrelated to this bill's subject. Ivan Bartoš and Hana Ančincová carry only the generic, zero-value graph 'OSVČ' marker common across many sponsors in this and the prior batch, with no distinguishing financial substance. Richterová, Pipášová, Šmída, and Volpe carry no recorded money ties. This bill, unlike a subsidy or procurement measure, does not direct money to any named entity — it is a prudential investment-limit change whose beneficiary class (PE/VC managers generally, pension savers generally) is diffuse and unconnected to the sponsors' graph-recorded financial interests. Symmetric absence-of-conflict finding, consistent with batch-001 doctrine.

citations.claim: Tisk 86 amends 427/2011 §3 (new definitions of 'fond soukromého kapitálu' and 'fond rizikového kapitálu'), §98 odst. 1 písm. g) and odst. 3 (permits the mandatory conservative fund to hold EU/OECD-regulated-market equities for the first time), and §100 odst. 2 písm. k) and new odst. 8 (permits participant funds to hold PE/VC fund securities up to a 10% asset cap). No fiscal impact on public budgets stated. Effective 1 Jan 2027. Signed by Richterová, Bartoš, Ančincová, Pipášová, Martínková Španihelová, Šmída, Volpe, Prague 16 Jan 2026.

Legislative history: distributed as print 86/0 on 22 Jan 2026; government issued a 'nesouhlas' (disapproval) position (print 86/1, 25 Feb 2026); Organizational Committee recommended proceeding 4 Mar 2026 with rapporteur Benjamin Činčila and the Budget Committee (RV) as guarantor; one amendment pending, no first reading as of 24 July 2026.

Sibling tisk 71 (same sponsor group, same amended statute) touches only §60 odst. 3-4 and §192 odst. 3 písm. a) of 427/2011 — confirmed by direct reading to share zero provisions with tisk 86's §3/§98/§100 changes, so no drafting collision exists between the two bills despite the shared siblingCollisionGroups flag.
The amended supplementary-pension-savings statute is zákon č. 427/2011 Sb., o doplňkovém penzijním spoření — a real, in-force Czech law.

Sponsor Lenka Martínková Španihelová's recorded money tie, MATURUS, o.p.s. (~1.2M CZK), is a nonprofit graphic-design social enterprise employing people with disabilities, not a pension company, asset manager, or investment fund.
Sponsors Ivan Bartoš and Hana Ančincová hold only the generic, zero-value graph 'OSVČ' self-employment marker, recorded at 0 CZK with no company-specific detail.
